_README: Published Super Two cutoffs, entered by hand. This is to super_two.py
what data/reference_service_time.json is to the service-time math: the
only check that does not come from this project's own data.
WHY IT MATTERS HERE PARTICULARLY: the computed cutoffs land in the
2.11-2.14 band with no tuning, which looks like confirmation and is
not. Every serious bug in this project so far has been a plausible
belief about MLB's rules, encoded, wrong -- and a number that lands
where you expected is exactly how those survived. A published figure
is the only thing that can actually settle it.
WHERE TO FIND THEM: public reporting publishes the cutoff each
offseason. Enter it exactly as published, e.g. "2.132". The figure
is posted for the class that just finished that season.
`season` is the season the class finished, NOT the offseason label. A
cutoff reported in November 2025 for the 2025-26 arbitration class has
season 2025 here.
Rows with `published` left null are skipped, so partial completion is
fine. `ours` is filled in by the validator at run time and is not
input -- do not paste computed values into `published`, that would
make the check vacuous.

ENTERED 2026-10-26, seasons 2021-2025. Seasons 2009-2020 were added 2026-11-07 from the published offseason figures. The 2026 row (2.133) was added 2026-11-10 from public reporting dated October 28, 2026. The season/offseason labelling is the one thing to get right and search summaries get it wrong: several described a report dated 2024/11 as being 'for the 2025 season'. The report date is the evidence -- the figure is posted in November for the class that has just finished that season -- and each report's own 'up from'/'down from' claim corroborates its neighbour, so the five form a chain rather than five independent guesses.

note: Official cutoff for the class that finished 2026. Public reporting on Oct 28, 2026, citing Kiley McDaniel of ESPN. The Associated Press the same week named the last two players at 2 years, 133 days.
Reported November 2025 (ESPN and AP, 34 Super Twos; Matt McLain last above the line). An earlier public report had trailed it at 2.140; the November figure is the official one.
Public reporting. Reported as up from 2.118 the previous winter, which corroborates the 2023 row.
Public reporting. Reported as down from 2.128, corroborating 2022.
Public reporting. Ronald Blum, Associated Press; reported as a slight increase on 2.116, corroborating 2021.
